description: Golden RAG cases for FanCare Assistant. expected_behavior: answer = full grounded answer; partial = answer the covered part and say what is missing; refuse = say the information is not available (or decline off-topic). expected_chunk_ids are the gold evidence passages.

cases.question: What Wi-Fi frequency does the fan need?
cases.expected_output: Corvane smart fans connect to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; 5 GHz networks are not supported.

cases.question: How do I put the fan into pairing mode?
cases.expected_output: Turn the fan off and on at the wall switch three times within 10 seconds. The fan beeps twice and the status light blinks quickly; pairing mode stays open for 3 minutes.

cases.question: How many phones can be connected to the fan over Bluetooth at the same time?
cases.expected_output: Up to 4 phones can be paired over Bluetooth at the same time; a fifth is refused until one is removed.

cases.question: What battery does the remote control use?
cases.expected_output: The remote uses one CR2032 coin battery, which lasts about 12 months.

cases.question: How do I pair the remote with my fan?
cases.expected_output: Restore power, then within 60 seconds hold Speed 1 and Speed 6 together for 5 seconds (Low and High on Basic models). The light blinks twice when pairing succeeds; if 60 seconds pass, power cycle and try again.

cases.question: What does error E7 mean?
cases.expected_output: E7 means a firmware update failed. The fan automatically rolls back to the previous firmware; retry the update when the fan has a stable Wi-Fi connection.

cases.question: My fan stopped and shows E2. What should I do?
cases.expected_output: E2 means overheat: thermal protection stopped the motor. The fan resets automatically after a 15-minute cool-down. Never attempt to bypass the thermal protection.

cases.question: What does E9 mean and how do I fix it?
cases.expected_output: E9 means the supply voltage is out of range; the fan needs 110 to 130 V. It is usually caused by a dimmer or variable-speed wall control, so replace it with a standard on/off switch and contact an electrician if E9 continues.

cases.question: My ceiling fan wobbles a lot at high speed. How do I fix it?
cases.expected_output: Switch off and tighten all blade and mounting bracket screws, then use the balancing kit: clip the weight halfway along each blade in turn, run the fan, and stick the weight where the wobble is smallest. Stop using the fan if it still wobbles severely.

cases.question: How long does a firmware update take?
cases.expected_output: About 6 minutes. Do not switch the fan off at the wall during the update. With Auto Update enabled, updates install at 03:00 local time.

cases.question: Which voice assistants work with Corvane fans?
cases.expected_output: Amazon Alexa and Google Home. Basic (BS) models are not supported because they have no Wi-Fi.

cases.question: I bought my fan last month. How long is the motor covered under warranty?
cases.expected_output: Fans bought on or after 1 January 2025 are covered by the 2025 policy, which covers the motor for 5 years from purchase.

cases.question: How long do I have to return a fan?
cases.expected_output: You can return a fan within 30 days of the delivery date; seasonal promotions can extend this window.

cases.question: Is there a fee if I opened the box but did not install the fan and want to return it?
cases.expected_output: Yes, opened but not installed fans with all parts are refunded minus a 10 percent restocking fee. The fee is waived for deliveries between 15 November and 31 December 2026 under the holiday notice.

cases.question: How long does it take to get my refund?
cases.expected_output: Refunds go back to the original payment method within 5 to 7 business days after the returned fan is inspected at the warehouse.

cases.question: Can I cancel my order after it has shipped?
cases.expected_output: No. Orders can only be cancelled while their status is Processing. After that, use the returns process.

cases.question: Which countries do you ship to?
cases.expected_output: Corvane ships to the United States and Canada only.

cases.question: How high above the floor do the fan blades need to be?
cases.expected_output: At least 7 ft (2.1 m) above the floor, and at least 18 inches (46 cm) from walls and sloped ceiling surfaces.

cases.question: How often should I clean the blades, and what should I use?
cases.expected_output: Every 3 months, with the fan off, using a dry or slightly damp microfibre cloth. Do not use solvents, abrasive cleaners or furniture polish.

cases.question: Which downrod length do I need for a 10 ft ceiling?
cases.expected_output: An 18-inch downrod.

cases.question: What fan size do I need for a 200 square foot room?
cases.expected_output: For 145 to 225 sq ft, choose a 50 to 54 inch blade span.

cases.question: How do I remove all phones paired over Bluetooth?
cases.expected_output: Hold the Fan Off and Light buttons on the remote together for 10 seconds. The fan beeps three times and forgets all paired phones; Wi-Fi settings are not affected.

cases.question: Which Wi-Fi bands does the fan support, and is it Wi-Fi 6 certified?
cases.expected_output: It supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only (not 5 GHz). The documentation does not say whether it is Wi-Fi 6 certified.

cases.question: What battery does the remote use, and how much does a replacement remote cost?
cases.expected_output: The remote uses a CR2032 battery. The documentation does not list the price of a replacement remote, though remotes are covered as accessories under the warranty.
cases.notes: DOC-06:4 (replacing the battery) also states CR2032; added after the first smoke run showed it was valid evidence missing from the label.

cases.question: How long is the motor warranty on a fan bought in 2025, and can I buy an extended warranty?
cases.expected_output: Under the 2025 policy the motor is covered for 5 years. The documentation does not mention an extended warranty you can buy.

cases.question: How do I set the fan up for winter, and what RPM should it run at?
cases.expected_output: On DC models use Reverse so the fan turns clockwise at low speed and pushes warm air down. The documentation does not give an RPM figure.

cases.question: Does the Corvane Home app work on iPhone, and is there an Apple Watch app?
cases.expected_output: Yes, the app needs iOS 16 or later. The documentation does not mention an Apple Watch app.

cases.question: How many schedules can I create, and can they sync with Google Calendar?
cases.expected_output: You can create up to 10 schedules per fan. The documentation does not mention Google Calendar sync.

cases.question: How long does standard shipping take, and which courier delivers in Canada?
cases.expected_output: Standard shipping takes 3 to 7 business days. The documentation does not say which courier delivers in Canada.

cases.question: How quiet are the Hush fans, and how many watts do they use at top speed?
cases.expected_output: Hush models are rated at 28 dB or less at speed 1. The documentation does not state power use at top speed.

cases.question: Does the fan support Matter or Thread?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation.

cases.question: Where are Corvane fans manufactured?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation.

cases.question: Can I control the fan with IFTTT?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation.

cases.question: What is the maximum RPM of the SkyWhirl 60?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation.

cases.question: Does Corvane offer a professional installation service?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation. The installation guide recommends a licensed electrician if you are not comfortable with wiring.

cases.question: What is the capital of France?
cases.expected_output: Sorry, I can only help with questions about Corvane ceiling fans.

cases.question: Write me a Python function that sorts a list.
cases.expected_output: Sorry, I can only help with questions about Corvane ceiling fans.

cases.question: Is a Corvane fan better than a Hunter fan?
cases.expected_output: Sorry, I can only help with questions about Corvane ceiling fans.

cases.question: Can I pay for my fan in monthly instalments?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation.

cases.question: How much does the Loft 72 weigh?
cases.expected_output: I don't have that information in the Corvane documentation.

cases.question: My fan shows E3 and I bought it in March 2025. Is the repair covered by warranty?
cases.expected_output: E3 is a motor sensor fault, and the sensor counts as part of the motor. Fans bought from 2025 fall under the 2025 policy, which covers the motor for 5 years, so it is covered until March 2030 (subject to the policy exclusions).

cases.question: My fan shows E4 and I bought it in June 2023. Is a replacement receiver covered?
cases.expected_output: If E4 persists the receiver module needs replacing, and the receiver counts as electronics. A June 2023 purchase falls under the 2022 policy, which covers electronics for 1 year, so coverage ended in June 2024 and the receiver is no longer covered.
cases.notes: DOC-12:1 states that 2022-2024 purchases stay on the 2022 policy, the routing step of this question; added after the first smoke run.

cases.question: My remote stopped working on a fan I bought in February 2026. What should I try, and is a replacement remote covered?
cases.expected_output: Replace the CR2032 battery first; if the remote's light flashes but the fan does not react, re-pair it; if it does not flash, the remote is faulty. Remotes are accessories, covered for 1 year under the 2025 policy, so a February 2026 purchase is covered until February 2027.

cases.question: The app shows E8 and my fan light stopped working. I bought the fan in May 2025 and registered it. Is it still covered?
cases.expected_output: E8 is a light driver fault, and the light kit is an accessory. Accessories are covered for 1 year, and registration only extends electronics, so the light kit coverage ended in May 2026.

cases.question: I want a fan for an open patio where rain can reach it. Which fan family should I choose, and how do I clean it?
cases.expected_output: Only TerraBreeze (TB) models are wet-rated for outdoor use where rain can reach them. Clean them with a damp cloth and mild soap, and never use a pressure washer or hose on the motor housing.

cases.question: Setup keeps failing at 'Connecting to Wi-Fi' and then the app shows E5. What is going on?
cases.expected_output: Setup failing at Connecting to Wi-Fi is most often a 5 GHz-only or combined-band network; enable a separate 2.4 GHz network name or turn off 5 GHz temporarily, and check the password. E5 means the 3-minute pairing window expired, so enter pairing mode again before retrying.

cases.question: Can I control my Basic 52 with Alexa?
cases.expected_output: No. Basic models have no Wi-Fi module, and voice assistants are not supported on Basic models.

cases.question: I use my SkyWhirl in my cafe. I bought it in April 2025. How long is the motor covered?
cases.expected_output: Fans used in commercial premises such as cafes are covered for 1 year on all components under the 2025 policy, so the motor is covered until April 2026, not 5 years.

cases.question: How long is the motor warranty?
cases.expected_output: It depends on the purchase date: 5 years for fans bought on or after 1 January 2025 (2025 policy), and 3 years for fans bought between 1 March 2022 and 31 December 2024 (2022 policy).

cases.question: I bought my fan in August 2024. How long are the electronics covered?
cases.expected_output: An August 2024 purchase is covered by the 2022 policy, which covers electronics for 1 year, so until August 2025. The 2-year electronics coverage only applies to purchases from 2025.

cases.question: I bought my fan in 2023. Does registering it extend the warranty?
cases.expected_output: No. Fans bought in 2023 are under the 2022 policy, where registration does not extend any coverage. The registration bonus (one extra year of electronics coverage) only applies under the 2025 policy.

cases.question: We bought a fan for our office in 2023. Is it under warranty?
cases.expected_output: No. A 2023 purchase falls under the 2022 policy, which does not cover fans used in commercial premises. (The 2025 policy gives commercial fans 1 year, but only for purchases from 2025.)

cases.question: Can I return a fan 40 days after it was delivered?
cases.expected_output: Normally no, the return window is 30 days from delivery. However, fans delivered between 15 November and 31 December 2026 can be returned until 31 January 2027 under the holiday notice, so it depends on the delivery date.

cases.question: Someone on the forum said to turn Breeze mode off and use speed 1 for the quietest bedroom. Is that official Corvane advice?
cases.expected_output: That is a community tip, not official advice. It is consistent with the official documentation: Breeze mode varies the speed randomly, and DC models are rated at 32 dB or less at speed 1.

cases.question: Does the fan support 5 GHz Wi-Fi?
cases.expected_output: No. Corvane fans connect to 2.4 GHz networks only; 5 GHz is not supported.

cases.question: Does the fan work with Apple HomeKit?
cases.expected_output: The documentation only lists Amazon Alexa and Google Home; it does not mention Apple HomeKit, so I can't confirm HomeKit support.

cases.question: Can I install a SkyWhirl in a bathroom with a shower?
cases.expected_output: No. Only TerraBreeze models are wet-rated; all other models, including SkyWhirl, are for dry indoor locations and must not be installed in bathrooms with showers.

cases.question: Can I install a TerraBreeze fan inside a sauna?
cases.expected_output: The documentation says TerraBreeze models are wet-rated for outdoor use and that other models must not be installed in saunas, but it does not say whether TerraBreeze can be used in a sauna, so I can't confirm that.

cases.question: How many people can control the fan from their phones over Wi-Fi?
cases.expected_output: You can share the fan with up to 6 household members in the Corvane Home app. The limit of 4 phones applies to Bluetooth pairing.

cases.question: What does error E10 mean?
cases.expected_output: The documentation lists error codes E1 to E9 only; E10 is not documented.

cases.question: What warranty applies to a fan I bought in January 2022?
cases.expected_output: The documented policies cover purchases from 1 March 2022 onwards, so I don't have information about the warranty for a January 2022 purchase.

cases.question: Can I use reverse mode on the Basic 52?
cases.expected_output: No. Basic models use an AC motor and have no reverse function.

cases.question: Can I use a dimmer switch to control the speed of a DC fan?
cases.expected_output: No. Do not connect the fan to a dimmer or variable-speed wall control; use a standard on/off switch. A dimmer can cause error E9.

cases.question: Does the remote take a CR2025 battery?
cases.expected_output: No, the remote uses a CR2032 coin battery.

cases.question: Can I return an installed fan if it was delivered during the 2026 holiday period?
cases.expected_output: No. The holiday notice extends the return window, but installed fans are still not returnable; use the warranty for faults.

cases.question: Does registering my fan in the app extend the motor warranty?
cases.expected_output: No. Under the 2025 policy, registering within 60 days extends electronics coverage by 1 year only; motor and accessory coverage are not extended.
